items.title: 68533_Sam Jones oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions Slide Hampton only in the context of the Interviewer's conversation with him ('Slide Hampton and I was talking about this...'). The Interviewee (Sam Jones) does not speak about Slide Hampton or indicate any personal interaction.

ctx.x: But, you see, you find those guys, well, it's a common thing in New Orleans, man, don't you see, because, uh, their fathers were fine musicians and their father was a teacher and they send them to--after they come home from a teacher their father teaches, you see, so that makes them fine musicians down there. But you see, those folks, man, they don't ever leave, see they stay, stay down there man. You know, because, uh,--

But you know the thing that I've always felt too, saying one of the things that that happened right here in New York it seems to me-I mean this is just my perception of it--I don't know how you feel about it. But, Slide Hampton and I was talking about this about a year ago, and Slide was saying, he said, one of the things that I really have...New York about is it cats are willing to tell a kid that that he sounds good and then turn him around behind his back and talk about him like a dog. Why don't the cat just…

everybody say look at that jive motherfucker, you know, he's--who does he think he is. And there's all kinds of --these cats get into those kind of little bags, you know. Whereas...jam session used to be going on like if you got up on the stage and your shit wasn't correct the cat would tell you, I mean, very harshly, and might even kick your ass--
